title: Strategic plan, winter sidewalks and inclusionary zoning
subtitle: Heritage permit delegation, Bill 109 planning changes, zoning amendments, 2022 financial statements, watermain tender and an axe-throwing ban.
overview: Council approved the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan {{vote:m6}} and backed a package of winter sidewalk service enhancements {{vote:m9}}. Staff will add the enhancements to the 2024-2026 budgets for consideration. Staff said the changes aim to cut sidewalk clearing time from about 72 hours to 48 hours, with the new services expected to start in the 2024 winter season. Council also directed staff to use an Inclusionary Zoning discussion paper as the basis for consultation and draft policies, working with Kitchener, Cambridge and the Region {{vote:m10}}.

On planning, Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 44 to respond to Bill 109 {{vote:m14}}. That included delegating minor by-law and parking exemption authority to the Director of Planning and hiring two senior development planners. Council also approved general zoning amendments, including changes for additional dwelling units and coach houses {{vote:m13}}, and delegated heritage permit decisions to the Director of Planning {{vote:m12}}.

Council awarded a watermain lining tender {{vote:m7}}, funded Laurel Creek culvert repairs {{vote:m8}} and approved the 2022 financial statements {{vote:m11}}. It asked staff to update the Parks by-law to expressly prohibit axe throwing {{vote:m15}}. A closed session was held earlier in the day; the minutes record no public decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved the City's Strategic Plan for 2023-2026, with implementation, performance measures and community conversations to follow.
Council approved the recommended winter sidewalk service enhancements and directed staff to add them to the 2024-2026 operating and capital budgets for consideration.
Council directed staff, with Kitchener, Cambridge and the Region, to consult on the policy directions in the discussion paper and draft Official Plan and zoning provisions.

Council adopted the housekeeping amendment, approved a procedure for lapsing development applications, delegated minor by-law and parking exemption powers, and approved hiring two senior development planners.
Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-01, updating rules on additional dwelling units and coach houses, Northdale holding provisions and other corrections.
Council delegated authority to the Director of Planning or a designate to consent to and grant permits for alterations to designated heritage properties.
Council awarded the Highpoint Avenue CIPP watermain lining tender to Fer-Pal Construction Ltd. for a total of $1,585,747.45.
Council directed staff to return with an update to the Parks by-law that expressly prohibits axe throwing.

debate: On the Strategic Plan, councillors praised its action focus and its links to past plans. One councillor asked why specific language on anti-Palestinian racism raised by a delegate at the draft stage was not included. Staff said the plan avoids naming particular groups, and that action plans may address such needs.

On winter sidewalks, delegates supported the package as a step toward full city-wide clearing. One delegate urged clearing regional-road sidewalks in all zones and swapping the timing with by-law enforcement funding. Another asked for a lower snowfall trigger than eight centimetres. Staff said they would take the swap idea back, and noted that moving enforcement funding would complicate keeping the current three officers.

Councillors also raised adding clearing around school zones as a budget menu item. Finance staff said service enhancements are being weighed together, at about two percent a year across several items, and that these ideas would be considered in the budget process.

On inclusionary zoning, councillors worried that allowing affordable units off-site could produce luxury-only buildings and concentrate affordable units away from Uptown. They suggested a further requirement for off-site options. Staff agreed to revisit the off-site approach and the classification of some station areas. Staff also said a builders' association argument about costs is managed through low initial set-aside rates.

In the zoning hearing, a resident said construction noise from owner-run renovations, which can run seven days a week, harms neighbours. Staff said the building code does not let the City regulate construction noise, and councillors asked staff to look at the noise by-law, with community engagement.
